stories.summary: Senate Republicans are staring into the abyss. It could be very difficult for them to reclaim the chamber in two years, especially if Democrats win still-uncalled races in Mississippi and Alaska. Those seats may not be decided for days, and would represent the potential 55th and 56th seats of a Democratic majority — the largest since the first two years of Barack Obama’s presidency. Republicans’ top Senate pickup opportunities in 2028 are Arizona, Georgia, Ohio, New Hampshire, Pennsylvania, and Nevada. Democrats have solid winning streaks in all of those states except Pennsylvania and Ohio. It could get even worse for Republicans trying to take the chamber back in two years: Democrats have pickup opportunities of their own in Wisconsin and North Carolina, and GOP-held seats in South Carolina, Iowa, Kansas and Alaska. — Burgess Everett

The last ballots are still being totaled, but many of the politicians from working-class backgrounds who ran won, or seem poised to win. During national elections, we often hear a lot about the rare candidates who had working-class jobs. If you follow politics, you’re likely to know that Maine’s newly elected Senator Troy Jackson was a logger, or that New York Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez was a bartender. articles.summary: The Democratic wave began in the streets of the Bronx, with an unheralded Assemblymember asking New Yorkers why they voted for Donald Trump during the weeks following the 2024 presidential election. It picked up steam in 2025, as a congressmember from that borough barnstormed the country into deep red districts, dispelling the myth of a true political realignment towards incipient fascism. On Tuesday, it crashed across the country in the form of an absolute Republican wipeout, with Democrats making historic gains in both New York and in states that had been written off generationally for Democrats, including Texas, Kansas, and Iowa.
